# The bindgen skill's build modes, as the bundling migration met them

Status: `open`.

## Signal

Skills that cannot be followed as written (`evolution` §2), met by the campaign's bundling
migration (`crustify/migrations/bundled-sys`, `6f38b8596` … `e11d5b3ae`, 2026-11-13), which laid
the raw bindings out as `bindgen` (crustify `63b92be`) describes:

1. **Shared mode cannot serve a target built with hidden visibility.** Build modes says shared
   mode builds `c/` "the same way" and ships the libraries through an `$ORIGIN` rpath (lines
   111, 124–129). libgit2's CMake adds `-fvisibility=hidden` (`c/cmake/DefaultCFlags.cmake:131`),
   so its shared library lacks the 42 internal items the bindings reach; the migration's build
   script fails shared mode naming them. The paragraph that handles this (lines 143–148) names
   system mode alone.
2. **"The generated modules' doctests are off" (lines 64–65)** has no direct means once the
   bindings are modules of the safe crate: rustdoc has no per-module switch. The migration
   compiles doctests from a `cfg(doctest)` copy of the bindings whose C doc comments are plain
   comments.
3. **Package contents (lines 198–200)**: "nothing else of the repository" is unreachable, since
   cargo always adds `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml.orig` and `.cargo_vcs_info.json`; the migration
   also packages `README.md`.
4. **Bundled mode's prerequisites**: bundled mode builds `c/` against the system's out-of-tree
   libraries, which a host may lack (this one has no PCRE2 or zlib development files); the
   skill says nothing of how a dependent supplies them (`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`/`PKG_CONFIG_PATH`
   here).

The `git2` link unit's scaffold (`f9a02dc65`, `44e95b76d`, 2026-11-13), the CLI executable, met
four more:

5. **"An empty allowlist generates nothing" (Generation)**: bindgen still writes its one-line
   banner, and the update path deleted an empty `static_fns.c` that Layout lists as committed;
   the build script now writes it empty.
6. **An executable link unit in bundled mode**: no target of the build system builds an
   executable's objects without linking it; the build script runs the compile commands the
   build system records for the CLI's TUs (`compile_commands.json`) and archives them, which is
   not "built by the target's own build system" as Build modes says.
7. **An executable link unit in shared and system modes**: neither mode says what to do with a
   link unit no library holds; the build script refuses its feature, naming the modes that serve it.
8. **A type `external.txt` re-exports must be bound in the owning link unit**: the CLI's headers
   name `git_str`, which `sys::libgit2` did not bind, so the scaffold added it to libgit2's
   allowlist; Extending says a batch extends its own link unit's input and nothing else, which
   leaves this cross-unit case unsaid.

## Destination

The spec: `bindgen` (Generation, Build modes, Publishing).

## Change

To be drafted: shared mode joins system mode's rule (it cannot serve once the bindings reach
what the shared library hides, and the build fails naming it); the doctests are compiled from a
copy of the bindings with C comments as plain comments; the package holds the layout, `src/`,
the files of `c/` the bundled build reads, and the files cargo itself adds; bundled mode finds
the out-of-tree libraries as the target's build system does, and says so when one is missing.

## Validation

The migration's build script and gates are the rerun: shared mode fails with the 42 items named,
doctests pass, `cargo package` packages and verifies (650 files), bundled builds with the
side campaigns' installs on the search paths.

## Review

Pending.

# Claude Code refuses --dangerously-skip-permissions as root without this.
    IS_SANDBOX=1
# BorrowSanitizer supplies its matched Rust/Clang/LLVM toolchain. Add the
# remaining generic build tools; `nasm`/`yasm` avoid a source build before a
# crypto audit can start. libclang-dev supports ordinary bindgen builds; bsan
# selects its own matched libclang when it instruments a build.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates unzip xz-utils file lld libclang-dev \
        jq ripgrep \
        nasm yasm autoconf automake libtool m4 python3 \
RUN mkdir -p /opt/bsan-shim \
    && printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' \
         'exec env RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=bsan CARGO=/root/.cargo/bin/cargo /root/.cargo/bin/cargo-bsan "$@"' \
       > /opt/bsan-shim/cargo-bsan \
    && chmod +x /opt/bsan-shim/cargo-bsan

# bindgen for the raw bindings. It dlopens libclang at run time and clang-sys
# looks for the unversioned soname, so the search has to be pinned: this system
# carries libclang 18 (the base) AND libclang 23 (installed above for MSan's
# compiler-rt), and an unpinned bindgen may bind either. 18 is the base image's
# own clang, so it matches the headers everything else here is built against.
# bindgen only parses declarations, so it does not need to agree with the LLVM
# rustc or bsan codegen against.
#
# Installed before CARGO_HOME moves to the /work volume, so the binary lives in
# the image layer at /root/.cargo/bin and survives a fresh volume.
ENV LIBCLANG_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm-18/lib
RUN cargo install bindgen-cli --locked

# CodeQL CLI, for wavefront's extraction queries. GitHub publishes this bundle
# for x86-64 Linux but not native Linux ARM64, so an ARM image ships without it

BorrowSanitizer's `bsan` toolchain aside, and the formatter's unstable options need
nightly: a nightly pinned by date, recorded in the workspace manifest as
`[workspace.metadata.crustify] nightly = "nightly-<date>"`, and named explicitly wherever it
runs. A toolchain is moved forward only between waves, in a
commit of its own.

Every crate uses Rust edition 2024, with the workspace's `rust-version` set to the pinned

inherits the workspace's lints with `[lints] workspace = true`.

#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;

[package]
name = "libgit2-crustify"
description = "Safe Rust wrappers over libgit2's public API."
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
publish.workspace = true
# The raw bindings' link metadata, which dependents' build scripts read as `DEP_GIT2_*`.
links = "git2"
build = "build.rs"
# The packaged crate: the safe crate, its raw bindings and the C its bundled build reads
# (crustify's `bindgen` skill, Publishing).
include = [
    "/Cargo.toml",
    "/build.rs",
    "/README.md",
    "/src/**",
    "/sys/**",
    "/c/COPYING",
    "/c/CMakeLists.txt",
    "/c/cmake/**",
    "/c/include/**",
    "/c/src/CMakeLists.txt",
    "/c/src/cli/**",
    "/c/src/libgit2/**",
    "/c/src/util/**",
    "/c/deps/llhttp/**",
    "/c/deps/ntlmclient/**",
96:[[test]]
97-name = "ub_safe"
98-path = "tests/ub_safe/main.rs"
99-
100:[[test]]
101-name = "ub_unsafe"
102-path = "tests/ub_unsafe/main.rs"
103-
104:[[test]]
105-name = "equiv"
106-path = "tests/equiv/main.rs"
107-
108:[[test]]
109-name = "unit_pub"
110-path = "tests/unit_pub/main.rs"
111-
serde_json = "1"

[dev-dependencies]
# The campaign's tests and gates regenerate the bindings, and check them against the
# committed ones; the crate's dependents build from the committed bindings.
libgit2-crustify = { path = ".", features = ["bindgen"] }
trybuild = "1.0"

[lints]
workspace = true

[[test]]
name = "ub_safe"
path = "tests/ub_safe/main.rs"

[[test]]
name = "ub_unsafe"
path = "tests/ub_unsafe/main.rs"

[[test]]
name = "equiv"
path = "tests/equiv/main.rs"

[[test]]
name = "unit_pub"
path = "tests/unit_pub/main.rs"

[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["."]

[workspace.package]
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.100"
version = "0.1.0"
license = "GPL-2.0-only WITH GCC-exception-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/crustify-rs/libgit2-crustify"
publish = false

[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/glibc-crustify"]

[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox"]

nightly = "nightly-2026-10-08"
# The LLVM that generates the committed raw bindings, beside the bindgen pinned in

## 4. Builds

The target is built in the variants [`testing-builds`](../../verification/testing/builds/SKILL.md)'s Builds section lists:
`plain`, `coverage`, and one per sanitizer the campaign enables, by default every one the
toolchain supports. A sanitizer without a variant is one no batch tests for or runs under.

Each variant is configured as the settings' `target-config` asks, by default the target's
default configuration with its deprecated features disabled. A build compiles only what
its configuration selects, so the files it leaves out are listed with the reason; a part
left out that is worth covering gets a variant of its own.

The variants are recorded in `crustify/artifacts/build.json`, from
[`templates/build.json`](../../../templates/build.json): each an out-of-tree `dir` and the
`configure` and `build` commands run from it, with the file's `version` raised whenever a
command changes. The commands carry no job count, which each build takes as
[`concurrency`](../../operations/concurrency/SKILL.md) describes. The variants are built concurrently, and
each is smoke-tested once built. The shared variants are rebuilt after a landing changes
the compiled target.

Every symbol a batch binds or ports links from each variant. A target whose library
exports only its public API, through hidden visibility or a symbol map, exports none of
its internal functions, which are most of what a port campaign binds. Each of its variants
then also archives the objects of every link unit, a library's or an executable's, into
one static archive, each object once, by the
last step of its `build` command, and records it as the variant's `static`, a path
relative to its `dir`, which campaign mode links instead of the shared library, as
[`bindgen`](../../rust/bindgen/SKILL.md)'s Build modes section describes. Hidden visibility
keeps a symbol linkable within one link, so the archive reaches every function the C
defines with external linkage, in the target's own configuration, which stays as it is;
the target's own C consumers still link its shared library.

A campaign's target is the host's: Linux, with glibc, on a 64-bit architecture. Each variant links the
out-of-tree libraries the target uses from their side campaigns' local installs of the
same variant, as [`dependencies`](../../planning/dependencies/SKILL.md)'s Sources section describes,
with each library's install prefix in its `configure` command, and libc from the system.
Once a library's install first replaces the system's in a variant, the file's `version` is
raised and the baseline below runs again against it.

## 5. Baseline

The target's tests run on `plain`. A test that is unstable, or that needs infrastructure
the host does not provide, such as a network service or a test server, is disabled with
its reason. The dashboard records the baseline: passed out of total, the tests the suite
skipped by itself, and every disabled test. The campaign's final results must match it.

[features]
# Every link unit, so that the campaign's builds, lints and tests, which take the default
# features, cover each one the campaign ports.
default = ["libgit2", "git2"]
# One feature per link unit; each gates its module in src/lib.rs, and src/sys.rs's when the
# link unit is optional.
libgit2 = []
# The CLI (src/cli), whose C links libgit2's: the bundled build compiles its objects, and
# the `shared` and `system` modes, whose libraries hold none, refuse it.
git2 = ["libgit2"]
# Regenerates the raw bindings into OUT_DIR from the headers of the C a build links, in
# place of the committed ones; campaign mode checks them against the committed ones
# (crustify's `bindgen` skill, Build modes).
bindgen = ["dep:bindgen"]
# Builds `c/` as shared libraries in place of static ones.
shared = []

content.text:
I've reviewed all three changes: **change 1 is approved, changes 2 and 3 are rejected.** None of them weakens a check. I changed, committed and landed nothing. Because the changes are stacked, only `6aa6dc4` can be fast-forwarded now; `b3ebca7` and `ce6445d` need new commits, and new commits need a new review.

For all three, `python3 -I providers/claude/compose.py build` in a `git archive ce6445d` copy exits 0 and leaves `providers/claude/` unchanged. No skill text uses the target's names. The host paths cited are the image's documented ones, and the target's names appear only in the commit messages, which is fine.

## 1. `6aa6dc4`, the bindgen LLVM pin: approved
- **Evidence and code:** the proposal shows the signal (a BSan gate that couldn't run), and the new text at `bindgen/SKILL.md:101-107` matches `47b4662c9`:
  - the pin is an install prefix and version in `[workspace.metadata.crustify]` (`Cargo.toml:132-138`);
  - `pin_llvm` sets `LIBCLANG_PATH` and `CLANG_PATH` only when campaign mode regenerates (`build.rs:214`);
  - the build fails naming the pinned and found versions.
- **Rerun:** `cargo-variant.sh bsan test --workspace --no-run` built all 6 test executables without `CRUSTIFY_BINDINGS_UPDATE`. `/usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/clang` reports 18.1.3.
- **Weakening:** none. The byte-for-byte comparison is unchanged and the pin only adds a failure. A dependent's regeneration into `OUT_DIR` was never compared with anything and was unpinned before, so leaving it unpinned drops no check.
- **Entry:** the recurrence signal (one variant's driver failing the bindings comparison that another passes) is something a campaign would observe.
- **Optional fixes:**
  - Add the LLVM to the list of inputs the bindings follow from (`:52`).
  - Name the manifest keys, as `toolchain` names `nightly`.
  - `templates/docker/Dockerfile:187-188` still says bsan picks its own libclang, which campaign mode now overrides.

## 2. `b3ebca7`, ffibox's canonical path: rejected
- **The text contradicts itself:** `ffibox/SKILL.md:38` still gives `/opt/venv/share/ffibox` as the image's path. The new sentence at `:39-42` says the path has no symbolic link on it, yet the image makes that path a link (`templates/docker/Dockerfile:331-334`, to `/crustify-rs/ffibox`). A campaign that copies the example reproduces the defect.
- **Image docs disagree too:** `Dockerfile:315-316` and `templates/docker/README.md:126-127` still call `/opt/venv/share/<tool>` "the path a campaign's manifest names ffibox by".
- **Required fix:** change the example to the image's canonical checkout, `/crustify-rs/ffibox` (the Dockerfile's tools section, `:310-313`), and correct both image docs in the same change.
- **What holds:** the mechanism is right. trybuild 1.0.122 canonicalizes path dependencies (`run.rs:141`), and on a rerun of `ub_safe` compile-fail all five named snapshots pass with `$FFIBOX`. The entry's recurrence signal is observable. No weakening.

## 3. `ce6445d`, the build modes after bundling: rejected
All eight items have evidence, and five of them reran as the proposal says:
- shared mode fails naming 42 unexported items;
- `shared,git2` and `system,git2` both refuse the executable unit;
- bundled mode fails configuring with "PCRE2 support was requested but not found" until `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` names the side campaigns' installs;
- doctests pass (71 and 378).

**Required fixes:**
1. **Doctest copy (`bindgen/SKILL.md:67`):** it says the copy is written "beside the bindings it uses". The code writes it to `OUT_DIR/<unit>/bindings.doctest.rs` from whichever bindings the build uses (`build.rs:384`), and `src/sys.rs` includes it under `cfg(doctest)`. Layout's `src/sys.rs` row (`:32`) also leaves it out.
2. **Empty allowlist (`:74`):** "every link unit has the files the Layout lists" is false for the campaign, since `sys/libgit2/` has no `external.txt`. Narrow it to the two generated files.
3. **Executable's `main` (`:168-170`):** the second half of the sentence repeats the first, and the consequence the code records (`build.rs:101-112`) is missing. A test that references the TU defining `main`, directly or through another archive member, links a second `main` and fails. That TU's globals move to Rust exports first, and until then the affected TUs are reached through the variant's executable as a child process.
4. **Extending (`:198-201`):** the cross-unit exception sits between "nothing else" and the colon that opens the numbered steps, so the steps read as the exception's. It also leaves out the hand-written re-export in the unit's `src/sys.rs` module (`src/sys.rs:97`), which falls outside "its own link unit's input".
5. **Publishing (`:224`):** the new wording excludes `c/COPYING`, which the campaign packages (`Cargo.toml:19`) and which the bundled build never reads. The C's license files belong in the list.

**Weakening:** none. The shared-mode refusal turns what would have been a link-time failure into an earlier one with a named error. No gate builds shared mode: testing-gates' Regressions builds campaign mode, and packages in bundled mode.

The setup Builds edit and the entry's recurrence signals are acceptable. The proposal's Change section still says "to be drafted", and promises a "says so when one is missing" message that neither the text nor the code has; update it with the rework.

Proposals, changes and lessons from this run: none. The verdicts still need recording in each `PROPOSAL.md`'s Review section, which I left to the assistant since this run lands nothing. The BSan rerun left a `target/bsan` build directory in the campaign repository.
